module_title: Introduction to Peanut Butter & Nut Pastes

lessons.title: What is Peanut Butter? Varieties and Uses in African Cuisine
lessons.body: Peanut butter is made by grinding roasted peanuts into a smooth or chunky paste. In Africa, peanuts (groundnuts) are boiled, roasted, or fried, then ground with salt, sugar, or oil. The simplest version uses 100% peanuts. Commercial varieties add stabilizers (like palm oil or hydrogenated oil) to stop separation, and sweeteners (sugar, honey) or salt for taste. In West Africa, 'groundnut paste' is often unsweetened and used in soups like groundnut stew. In East Africa, peanut butter is spread on bread or mixed into uji (porridge). In Southern Africa, it's used in relishes and sauces. Varieties include smooth, crunchy (with chopped nuts added), natural (no additives), and flavored (chocolate, honey, chili). You can also make nut pastes from cashew, almond, or sesame (tahini). For a small business, start with smooth and crunchy peanut butter. Use local peanuts: in Nigeria, 'Kano groundnut' is popular; in Senegal, 'Touba groundnut'; in Malawi, 'CG7' variety. Roast at 160Â°C for 20-30 minutes until golden and oily. Grind while warm using a food processor or a local mill. Add 1-2% salt and 5-10% sugar if desired. For crunchy, stir in 10% chopped roasted peanuts. Uses in African cuisine: groundnut soup (Ghana, Nigeria), domoda (Gambia), peanut sauce with rice (Tanzania), kuli-kuli (Nigeria) from peanut paste, and as a snack with banana or cassava. In markets, sell in clean jars or sachets. Label with production date and ingredients. This lesson sets the foundation: know your product, its varieties, and how it fits local dishes.

lessons.title: Health Benefits and Nutritional Value of Peanut Butter
lessons.body: Peanut butter is a nutrient-dense food. A 2-tablespoon (32g) serving of natural peanut butter provides about 190 calories, 7-8g protein, 16g fat (mostly healthy unsaturated), 6-8g carbohydrates, and 2g fiber. It contains vitamin E, magnesium, potassium, and B vitamins. In Africa, where protein-energy malnutrition is a concern, peanut butter is a cheap protein source. The protein helps build muscles and repair the body. Healthy fats support brain function and keep you full. Fiber aids digestion and prevents constipation. However, peanut butter is high in calories, so portion control matters. Also, some people are allergic to peanutsâa serious condition. For a business, highlight health benefits: no cholesterol, good for heart health when eaten in moderation, and suitable for children over 2 years (not for infants due to choking risk and allergy). Avoid adding too much sugar or palm oil; keep it natural for health-conscious customers. In markets, you can promote 'no added sugar' or 'high protein' as selling points. Note that roasting reduces some nutrients but improves flavor and digestibility. Store in a cool, dark place; natural peanut butter separatesâstir before use. In African contexts, peanut butter is used in therapeutic foods like Plumpy'Nut for severe malnutrition. So your product can contribute to community health. But always follow hygiene: contaminated peanut butter can cause aflatoxin poisoning from moldy peanuts. Use only good-quality, dry peanuts. This lesson helps you explain to customers why your peanut butter is good for them, and how to make it safely.

lessons.title: Market Demand for Peanut Butter in Your Local Area
lessons.body: Before starting, check demand in your area. Walk around your neighborhood, local markets, schools, and shops. Ask: Do people already buy peanut butter? What brands? What price? In many African cities, demand for peanut butter is growing due to urbanization and busy lifestyles. For example, in Nairobi, a 500g jar of local peanut butter sells for KES 300-500. In Lagos, it's NGN 1,500-2,500. In Accra, GHS 20-30. But in rural areas, demand may be lower because people make their own. Target customers: urban families, students, health-conscious adults, and food vendors who use peanut butter in cooking. Also, schools and hospitals buy in bulk for feeding programs. Check competition: Are there big brands like Jif or local ones? What gaps? Maybe they don't offer unsweetened or organic. You can also sell to restaurants making groundnut soup. To estimate demand, count potential customers: if your town has 5,000 households and 10% buy peanut butter monthly, that's 500 jars per month. Start small: produce 20 jars per week, test the market. Use social media (WhatsApp, Facebook) to advertise. Offer free samples at markets. Price competitively: calculate your cost per jar (peanuts, jars, labels, labor, transport). If a 500g jar costs you 200 KES to make, sell at 350 KES for profit. Also consider seasonality: demand may rise during school terms or holidays. In Muslim areas, demand increases during Ramadan for groundnut soup. Keep records of sales to adjust production. This lesson gives you practical steps to research and understand your local market before investing money.

lessons.title: Overview of Nut Pastes: Groundnut, Cashew, Almond, and Sesame
lessons.body: Nut pastes are made by grinding nuts or seeds into a spreadable paste. Groundnut (peanut) paste is the most common in Africa. Cashew paste is made from roasted cashew nuts; it's creamy and slightly sweet. Cashew apples are also used, but the nut is key. In Tanzania, cashew paste is used in curries. Almond paste is made from almonds; it's expensive because almonds are imported in many African countries. But if you have local almond trees (e.g., in Morocco), it can be viable. Sesame paste (tahini) is made from hulled sesame seeds, roasted and ground. It's used in hummus, halva, and as a base for sauces. In Sudan, sesame paste is used in salads. Each paste has different oil content: groundnut has about 50% oil, cashew 44%, almond 50%, sesame 55%. This affects grinding: sesame needs longer grinding to release oil. For a small business, start with groundnut paste because peanuts are cheap and widely available. Then diversify: cashew paste for premium markets, sesame paste for Middle Eastern foods. Equipment: a good grinder (stone mill or stainless steel). For sesame, you may need to add a little oil to get a smooth paste. Roasting temperatures: groundnut 160Â°C, cashew 150Â°C, almond 150Â°C, sesame 180Â°C for 10-15 minutes. Always cool before grinding. Add salt or sugar to taste. Packaging: glass jars or food-grade plastic. Label with ingredients and date. Health benefits: cashew paste is rich in iron; almond paste in vitamin E; sesame paste in calcium. But all are high in calories. In African markets, groundnut paste dominates, but there is growing demand for variety. This lesson helps you understand options beyond peanut butter.

lessons.title: Legal and Regulatory Requirements for Food Processing in Your Country
lessons.body: Food processing businesses must follow government rules to ensure safety. In most African countries, you need to register your business with the companies commission (e.g., CAC in Nigeria, RDB in Rwanda, CIPC in South Africa). Then get a food handling license from the local health department or ministry of health. This involves an inspection of your premises: clean water, proper drainage, pest control, and separate areas for storage, production, and packaging. You also need food handler's certificates for yourself and workers, proving you've taken a hygiene course. In Kenya, you need a food safety license from the county government and a certificate from the Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS) for your product. In Ghana, the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) regulates. In Nigeria, NAFDAC registers food products. The process includes submitting samples for lab testing (for aflatoxin, bacteria, etc.). Fees vary: NAFDAC registration can cost NGN 50,000-100,000. KEBS certification may cost KES 20,000-50,000. Also, you must label your product correctly: list ingredients, net weight, production and expiry dates, batch number, and your contact details. No false health claims. For export, you need additional certifications like HACCP or ISO 22000. But for local sales, start with basic registration. Many small businesses operate informally, but formalizing helps you sell to supermarkets and schools. Also, pay taxes: VAT if turnover exceeds threshold. Keep records. This lesson is not legal advice; check with your local authorities. But knowing the steps saves you fines and builds trust with customers.

lessons.title: Setting Up a Small-Scale Peanut Butter Business: Initial Steps
lessons.body: To start a small peanut butter business, begin with a simple plan. First, calculate startup costs: a grinder (manual or electric) costs $100-500; a roasting pan or oven $50-200; jars and labels $50; initial peanuts $100; registration $100-300. Total: $400-1,200. You can start at home with a kitchen license. Next, source peanuts: buy in bulk from local farmers or markets. In Nigeria, a 50kg bag of groundnuts costs NGN 40,000-60,000. Ensure they are dry and free of mold. Test for aflatoxin using a simple kit if possible. Then, set up a production area: clean, with a table, grinder, and storage. Follow hygiene: wash hands, wear gloves and hairnets. Production steps: roast peanuts at 160Â°C for 20-30 minutes, cool, remove skins (optional), grind with salt and sugar (1-2% salt, 5-10% sugar), and jar. For crunchy, add chopped nuts. Label with name, ingredients, weight, date. Price: calculate cost per jar. Example: 1kg peanuts makes about 500g peanut butter. If peanuts cost $2/kg, jar and label $0.50, labor $0.50, total $3. Sell at $5 for 500g. Profit $2 per jar. Sell 20 jars per week = $40 profit. Scale up by selling to shops, schools, and online. Market via WhatsApp, Facebook, and local radio. Offer free samples. Reinvest profits in better equipment. Keep records of income and expenses. Join a cooperative or association for support. This lesson gives you a clear roadmap to launch your business with minimal resources.

quiz.q: What is the main ingredient in traditional African groundnut paste?
quiz.explanation: Groundnut paste is made from peanuts, which are also called groundnuts.

quiz.q: Which of these is a common use of peanut butter in West African cuisine?
quiz.explanation: Groundnut soup is a traditional West African dish that uses peanut butter or groundnut paste.

quiz.q: What is the ideal roasting temperature for peanuts to make peanut butter?
quiz.explanation: Roasting at 160Â°C for 20-30 minutes gives a golden color and good flavor without burning.

quiz.q: Which additive is commonly used in commercial peanut butter to prevent oil separation?
quiz.explanation: Palm oil or hydrogenated oil is added as a stabilizer to keep the peanut butter from separating.

quiz.q: How much protein is in a 2-tablespoon serving of natural peanut butter?
quiz.explanation: A 2-tablespoon serving of natural peanut butter provides about 7-8 grams of protein.

quiz.q: Which nutrient is peanut butter particularly rich in?
quiz.explanation: Peanut butter is a good source of vitamin E, an antioxidant.

quiz.q: Why should peanut butter not be given to infants under 2 years?
options: B) Choking risk and allergy potential
quiz.explanation: Infants may choke on thick peanut butter and are at risk of developing peanut allergies.

quiz.q: What is aflatoxin and why is it a concern in peanut butter production?
options: B) A poisonous substance from moldy peanuts
quiz.explanation: Aflatoxin is a toxic compound produced by molds on peanuts, which can cause liver damage.

quiz.q: Which of these is a good way to estimate market demand for peanut butter?
options: B) Ask local shops and potential customers
quiz.explanation: Talking to local shops and customers gives real insights into demand and preferences.

quiz.q: In Nairobi, what is a typical price for a 500g jar of local peanut butter?
quiz.explanation: Local peanut butter in Nairobi typically sells for KES 300-500 per 500g jar.

quiz.q: Which group is most likely to buy peanut butter in urban areas?
quiz.explanation: Urban families with busy lifestyles often buy ready-made peanut butter for convenience.

quiz.q: What is a good first step before starting a peanut butter business?
options: B) Conduct a local market survey
quiz.explanation: A market survey helps you understand demand, competition, and pricing before investing.

quiz.q: Which nut paste is traditionally used to make tahini?
quiz.explanation: Tahini is a paste made from ground sesame seeds.

quiz.q: Which nut paste is typically the most expensive to produce in Africa?
quiz.explanation: Almonds are often imported in many African countries, making almond paste more expensive.

quiz.q: What is the approximate oil content of groundnut paste?
quiz.explanation: Groundnut paste contains about 50% oil, which helps make it spreadable.

quiz.q: Which nut paste is richest in calcium?
quiz.explanation: Sesame paste (tahini) is particularly high in calcium.

quiz.q: What equipment is essential for making nut pastes?
quiz.explanation: A grinder (stone mill or stainless steel) is needed to turn nuts into paste.

quiz.q: Why might you add a little oil when grinding sesame seeds?
options: B) To help achieve a smooth paste
quiz.explanation: Sesame seeds have high oil but may need extra oil to grind into a smooth paste.

quiz.q: Which government body regulates food products in Nigeria?
quiz.explanation: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) regulates food products in Nigeria.

quiz.q: What is a food handler's certificate?
quiz.explanation: A food handler's certificate shows you have taken a course in safe food handling.

quiz.q: Which of these must be included on a peanut butter label?
quiz.explanation: Labels must include production and expiry dates for food safety.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of registering your food business?
options: B) To ensure safety and build trust
quiz.explanation: Registration ensures your business meets safety standards and helps customers trust your product.

quiz.q: Approximately how much does it cost to register a food product with NAFDAC?
quiz.explanation: NAFDAC registration fees typically range from NGN 50,000 to 100,000.

quiz.q: What should you do before selling peanut butter to supermarkets?
options: B) Get necessary certifications and labels
C) Only have a verbal agreement
quiz.explanation: Supermarkets require proper certifications and compliant labeling.

quiz.q: What is a key step in setting up a small-scale peanut butter business?
quiz.explanation: Calculating startup costs helps you plan and avoid overspending.

quiz.q: How much peanut butter can you expect from 1kg of peanuts?
quiz.explanation: 1kg of peanuts yields about 500g of peanut butter after removing skins and oil loss.

quiz.q: What is a good pricing strategy for a new peanut butter business?
options: B) Calculate cost per jar and add profit margin
D) Give it away for free
quiz.explanation: Pricing should cover costs and include a reasonable profit margin.

quiz.q: Which of these is a low-cost marketing method for peanut butter?
quiz.explanation: Social media like WhatsApp and Facebook are low-cost and effective for local marketing.

quiz.q: Why is it important to keep records in a small food business?
options: B) To track income and expenses
quiz.explanation: Records help you understand profitability and make informed business decisions.

quiz.q: What is a cooperative or association useful for?
quiz.explanation: Cooperatives provide training, bulk buying, and marketing support for small businesses.
